trip.label: Fri 28 – Mon 31 August 2026
trip.weather: Late Aug: highs ~27 °C, lows ~17 °C. Sunset 19:40. Roughly 8 rain days in the month — pack one light layer for terraces at night.
trip.currency: Hungary uses the forint (HUF). ~390–400 HUF to €1. Cards work almost everywhere.

people.name: Areeb
people.note: Flight booked — details still to come.

people.name: Nhi
people.note: Flies home Sunday evening — one night shorter than the others.

people.name: Jacek
people.note: First one in, last one out.

flights.connection: 1 h 10 min in Warsaw — same terminal, domestic-to-Schengen, no passport control.

vote.blurb: Six places, all walkable to the bar strip, all under €450 for the whole three nights — for the group, not each. Tick everything you'd be happy with, not just your favourite.
vote.note: Prices are estimates from published rates, not live quotes — Airbnb's API is partner-only and Booking's needs an affiliate account, so nothing here can see the real number. Every card has a button that opens our exact dates and party size so you can.

groups.title: If all four of us go
groups.note: One apartment or family suite. Two hotel rooms for three nights blows the budget on its own, so these are all single-unit places with a kitchen or a kitchenette.

groups.title: If it's three of us
groups.note: A triple room works, which opens up proper hotels at the same money. Nicer rooms, no kitchen.

options.name: Bo33 Hotel Family & Suites
options.nearby: The quiet end of District VII, a few streets behind the Grand Boulevard. Keleti station is walkable, there's a supermarket on the corner, and the ruin bars are twelve minutes away — far enough that you actually sleep.
pros: One suite sleeps all four, so you pay for one unit
Kitchenette, and a small sauna and wellness room
cons: Residential block — nothing on the doorstep itself

options.name: Opera Garden Hotel & Apartments
options.nearby: A quiet side street directly behind the Opera House, just off Andrássy út. Cafés and the Opera on the doorstep, Oktogon five minutes up the avenue, the ruin bars about twelve minutes back down.
pros: Real apartments — kitchen, living room, space to sit that isn't a bed
The best-looking street of the six
cons: District VI is calm, so it's a proper walk back from the bars

options.name: Maverick City Lodge
options.nearby: On Kazinczy utca itself. Szimpla is sixty seconds away, Fat Mama is next door, and effectively everything on the picks board is inside five minutes on foot.
pros: Private en-suite rooms and apartments, not dorms — it's well designed
You can walk home from anywhere in seconds
cons: It's a lodge: young crowd, and it can be loud
You're sleeping above the bar strip — that's the point and the problem

options.name: Roombach Hotel Budapest Center
options.nearby: Between the Great Synagogue and Gozsdu Court. Five minutes to Szimpla one way, five minutes to Deák Ferenc tér and all three metro lines the other.
pros: Everything walkable, including the airport bus terminus
cons: Plain three-star rooms — clean, not charming

options.name: Hotel Museum Budapest
options.nearby: Beside the National Museum on the edge of the Palace Quarter — handsome nineteenth-century streets, quiet at night. The bars are about seven minutes north, the Central Market ten minutes south.
pros: Boutique hotel in a historic building — the nicest rooms in this price band
Quiet, and the neighbourhood is beautiful
cons: Just outside the action rather than in it
District VIII gets scruffier a few streets further east

options.name: Promenade City Hotel
options.nearby: On the Váci utca pedestrian street, two minutes from the river and ten from the Central Market Hall. Busy with tourists by day, genuinely calm at night.
pros: Smart four-star — the most grown-up option here
Riverside walks and the Danube panorama on the doorstep
cons: Váci utca restaurants are aimed squarely at tourists — eat elsewhere

airport.name: Liszt Ferenc International
airport.buffer_note: Schengen-to-Schengen — no passport queue. Allow ~25 min from wheels-down to standing at the bus stop, more if you checked a bag.

routes.label: Uber, Bolt or Főtaxi
routes.cost: ~€25–35 for the car, split between you

steps.text: One car from the terminal to the front door. Főtaxi is the official rank right outside arrivals; Uber and Bolt pickup are signposted.

routes.warning: The only sane option late at night, and cheap if you land together and share. Uber runs in Budapest through Főtaxi, so the car is a regulated yellow taxi at the regulated fare — same price as everyone else, just a nicer app.

routes.label: 100E Airport Express
routes.cost: 2,500 HUF for the 100E, plus one standard ticket for the last leg

steps.text: Bus 100E from Terminal 2 straight to Deák Ferenc tér. No transfer, every 6–10 min.
Onward from Deák Ferenc tér — the middle of the city, a few minutes from most places.

routes.label: 200E bus + M3 metro
routes.cost: Two standard tickets, ~900 HUF (~€2.30) — or nothing extra on a travelcard

steps.text: Bus 200E from Terminal 2 to Kőbánya-Kispest, the southern end of the M3 metro.
M3 metro north into town, then onward.

airport.night_note: Landing after ~22:30 the metro is closing (last M3 around 23:20). The 200E runs all night but terminates at Határ út after hours, and you would be stitching night buses together at 01:00 with luggage. Take a car.

getting_around.d: Gyöngyösi utca on the M3 (blue line). ~15 min to Deák Ferenc tér, the middle of everything.
Buy in the BudapestGO app. A 72-hour travelcard covers Fri–Mon and removes all thinking. Single tickets need validating; the app's don't.
Around 23:20. After that it is night buses (BudapestGO plans them for you) or a car — 15–20 min home from District VII.
District VII. Almost everything on the picks board is within ten minutes of Kazinczy utca on foot.
A 2.5 km park island in the middle of the Danube, on the tram 4/6 line — the easy answer to a free morning or a bag-drop gap.

money.d: If the card terminal offers to charge you in euros, say no. Dynamic currency conversion costs you 5–10% every time.
Barely needed. Keep ~10,000 HUF for markets and the odd cloakroom.
Use bank ATMs (OTP, K&H, Erste). Avoid the blue Euronet ones — bad rates, big fees.
10% is normal. Check the bill first — many District VII places already add a service charge.

phrases.en: Cheers! (never clink beer glasses — old habit, still holds)
In forints, please — the DCC killer
No, thank you — for anyone who approaches you on the street

essentials.d: 112 for everything — police, ambulance, fire. English is answered.

essentials.t: Apps to install before you fly
essentials.d: BudapestGO (tickets + journey planner), Bolt (taxis), and whatever the group chat is.
Swimwear worn underneath, flip-flops, a towel and a waterproof phone pouch. Drinks run on a deposit cup. 18+, bring ID.
Type C/F, 230 V — same as the rest of continental Europe.

slots.t: Open — baths, action, whatever wins the vote
Book it. District VII fills up on a Saturday.
Remember Parade at Budapest Park — same night
Open — last thing the four of you do together
Bags down, one last thing — Central Market is open till 18:00 on a Monday

clash.title: Saturday night collides
clash.body: Sparty runs Saturdays only, so Sat 29 Aug is the only shot at it. The Remember Parade at Budapest Park — ATB, Ferry Corsten, Umek, Da Hool, Brooklyn Bounce — is the same evening. You get one. The picks board is currently split.

airport.name: 100E airport ticket
airport.where: Purple BKK machine just outside the terminal exit, or in the BudapestGO app. Not sold on board — and a normal single or a travelcard is NOT valid on the 100E.

single.name: Standard single ticket
single.where: BudapestGO app, or a purple BKK machine — there is one at every metro entrance and most big stops. Paper tickets need validating at the little box; app tickets you activate before you board. Buying from the driver costs more.

travelcard.name: 72-hour travelcard
travelcard.where: BudapestGO or any purple machine. Covers Fri–Mon on metro, tram, bus and trolley — everything except the 100E. Pays for itself at about four journeys, and you stop thinking about tickets entirely.

none.name: No ticket needed
none.where: Uber and Bolt charge the card on file. A Főtaxi from the official rank runs on the meter — pay by card in the car.

apps.name: BudapestGO
apps.what: Buy and activate tickets on your phone, and plan any journey door to door with live departures. It replaces hunting for a ticket machine, and it's the only way to buy without cash or a card terminal.

apps.name: ntfy
apps.what: Install it, subscribe to our topic once, and anything anyone sends from the Ping tab lands on your phone as a notification. No account, no sign-up.
